title: Companies pledge free software and computing for AI in science
source_used: Blockchain.News and NVIDIA blog (Science|Business blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: On 15 Oct 2026 at the AI in Science Summit in Dublin the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative, linked to RAISE (Resource for AI Science in Europe).
NVIDIA is joining with open models, datasets and software, a free open-source courseware hub, and routes to European AI factories and supercomputing centres.
NVIDIA says it has released more than 250 open models, 250 open datasets and over 1,400 open-source software projects.
EuroHPC centres such as CINECA and JSC give academia and startups free access to NVIDIA GPU infrastructure for open research.
NVIDIA says 35 supercomputers are in development in Europe, to serve over 3 million researchers; Blockchain.News calls this a company-reported projection.
The post gives no new funding amounts for the initiative.
quote_evidence: Through the AI in Science Enablers campaign, we are turning this ambition into concrete commitments that give researchers the tools, expertise and resources they need to innovate.
The blog does not provide new funding amounts for the European AI in Science Enablers initiative itself.
why_it_matters_hint: Smaller labs and startups in Europe get easier access to tools and computing, but no new money was announced.
notes: Science|Business original blocked; read Blockchain.News and NVIDIA's own blog. Quote evidence for the Commissioner line is from the NVIDIA blog attributed to Ekaterina Zaharieva. Only NVIDIA's pledge was read in detail; other companies not verified.
